# Runtime Bug Burndown Ledger

This ledger tracks runtime-specific bug council findings for `slskNet.Runtime`. The scope is the .NET runtime library, its tests, package/release metadata, local scripts, and the example Web API only where it exercises runtime-facing path handling.

Statuses:

- `New`: discovered during static audit and awaiting confirmation.
- `Accepted`: confirmed or statically proven and queued for remediation.
- `Fixed`: remediated with local checks or regression tests.
- `Out of scope`: app-only, slskdN-specific, or not actionable in this runtime.

## Remediation Baseline

Run the local baseline before merging runtime hardening changes:

```bash
bash scripts/check-remediation-baseline.sh
```

The script verifies protocol parser count guards, frame and buffered-read limits, idempotent task completion, transfer cancellation/disconnect races, token bucket cancellation/disposal, peer descriptor fail-closed behavior, Web API path containment, sensitive token/key pattern absence, fork branding metadata, and this command reference.

## First Council Sweep

Date: 2026-05-05

Static discovery covered `src`, `tests`, `examples`, `bin`, and `.circleci`.

| ID | Domain | Finding | Evidence | Status | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RT-001 | Protocol parsing | Repeated protocol collections could trust negative or impossible counts before allocation/read loops. | `src/Messaging/Messages/**` collection readers and regression coverage in `tests/Soulseek.Tests.Unit/Messaging/Messages/ProtocolCountHardeningTests.cs`. | Fixed | Added `ProtocolCountReader` and wired parser count/matching-count validation into protocol responses. |
| RT-002 | Network lifecycle/concurrency | Message and initialization frames needed pre-read length limits to prevent oversized buffered allocations. | `src/Network/MessageFrameValidator.cs`, `src/Network/MessageConnection.cs`, `src/Network/ListenerHandler.cs`, and `tests/Soulseek.Tests.Unit/Network/MessageFrameValidatorTests.cs`. | Fixed | Centralized frame validation against rotated-obfuscation limits before reading frame bodies. |
| RT-003 | Transfer streams | Buffered connection reads could allocate caller-declared lengths that are inappropriate for message handshakes. | `src/Network/Tcp/Connection.cs` and transfer paths using stream overloads for large payloads. | Fixed | Added `MaximumBufferedReadLength` guard and retained stream read/write overloads for transfers. |
| RT-004 | Network lifecycle/concurrency | Duplicate disconnect, denied, failed, and cancellation callbacks could complete task sources more than once. | `src/SoulseekClient.cs`, `src/Network/Tcp/Connection.cs`, `src/Common/Waiter.cs`, and `src/SearchInternal.cs`. | Fixed | Runtime-owned task completion uses `TrySetResult`, `TrySetException`, or `TrySetCanceled` for race-prone paths. |
| RT-005 | Transfer streams | Download/upload races between transfer IO, disconnect, remote failure, and caller cancellation needed deterministic loser cancellation. | `src/SoulseekClient.cs` download/upload transfer loops. | Fixed | Transfer methods race IO against disconnect/remote-failure tasks and cancel the losing path with linked tokens. |
| RT-006 | Peer capability/signature trust | Capability descriptors must not be treated as authorization and signature verification must fail closed on malformed metadata. | `src/Ed25519PeerDescriptorSigner.cs`, `src/PeerCapabilityRegistry.cs`, and README compatibility notes. | Fixed | Verifier returns false for malformed signatures and catches verifier exceptions; registry stores descriptors as discovery hints only. |
| RT-007 | Obfuscation | Obfuscated peer/distributed/transfer frame parsing needed the same frame bounds as regular message parsing. | `src/Network/MessageConnection.cs`, `src/Network/ListenerHandler.cs`, and `src/Network/Tcp/ObfuscatedTransferConnection.cs`. | Fixed | Obfuscated lengths are decoded then validated before body allocation/read. |
| RT-008 | Example Web API path safety | Shared-directory and download-output paths could be vulnerable to prefix sibling escapes or absolute remote names if path containment was string-prefix only. | `examples/Web/api/Extensions.cs`, `examples/Web/api/Controllers/TransfersController.cs`, and `tests/Soulseek.Tests.Unit/WebApiPathSecurityTests.cs`. | Fixed | Added normalized root containment and safe relative output path helpers with regression tests. |
| RT-009 | Release/package metadata | Forked runtime package metadata could drift back to upstream Soulseek.NET branding. | `src/Soulseek.csproj`, `README.md`, `.circleci/config.yml`, and `docs/fork-runtime-changes.md`. | Fixed | Package id, project URLs, description, CI image, and README identify `slskNet.Runtime`. |
| RT-010 | Tests/tooling | Runtime hardening checks needed a durable command and registry so future audits do not depend on ad hoc shell history. | `scripts/check-remediation-baseline.sh` and this ledger. | Fixed | Added a Bash-only remediation baseline; no root `package.json` is required. |
| RT-011 | Sensitive material | Static audit should catch accidental embedded API tokens, private keys, or access tokens in runtime files. | `scripts/check-remediation-baseline.sh` secret scan over tracked text files. | Fixed | Baseline scans source, tests, examples, docs, scripts, bin, and `.circleci` for high-confidence key/token patterns. |
| RT-012 | Integration environment | Live Soulseek integration tests require external credentials and network access. | `tests/Soulseek.Tests.Integration/Settings.cs`. | Out of scope | Unit and build verification are required for this sweep; live integration is attempted only when credentials/network are intentionally provided. |
| RT-013 | App-only slskdN checks | slskdN app database, UI, auth, and deployment checks from app council workflows do not apply directly to this runtime library. | Runtime repo has no app database or deployment service surface. | Out of scope | Do not copy app-only remediation checks into this runtime. |

| RT-015 | Protocol parsing | Peer search/browse file parsers and transfer handshakes could accept negative 64-bit file sizes from malformed peer payloads. | `src/Messaging/MessageReaderExtensions.cs`, `src/Messaging/Messages/Peer/TransferRequest.cs`, `src/Messaging/Messages/Peer/TransferResponse.cs`, and peer parser tests. | Fixed | Reject negative parsed file sizes while preserving legacy Soulseek NS sign-extended unsigned 32-bit file-size normalization. |

| RT-017 | Protocol parsing | Type-1 obfuscated peer endpoint metadata could advertise unusable ports and be silently downgraded to clear peer endpoints. | `src/Messaging/Messages/ProtocolValueValidator.cs`, `ConnectToPeerResponse`, `UserAddressResponse`, and endpoint parser tests. | Fixed | Type-1 obfuscated endpoint metadata now validates advertised ports and rejects malformed values with `MessageException`. |
| RT-018 | Protocol parsing | Server user statistics and peer queue metadata accepted negative counters from malformed protocol payloads. | `ProtocolValueValidator`, user-data parsers, peer queue/search/info parsers, and `ProtocolScalarHardeningTests`. | Fixed | Added non-negative scalar validation for parsed speeds, upload/file/directory counts, free slot counts, queue lengths, and queue positions. |

| RT-029 | Example Web API request validation | Search and connect endpoints dereferenced missing request bodies or blank search text instead of returning `400`. | `SearchesController`, `ServerController`, and `WebApiRequestTests`. | Fixed | Example endpoints now validate request bodies, usernames, and normalized search terms before invoking runtime calls. |
| RT-030 | Example Web API token DTO | Token response properties dereferenced missing JWT claims and reparsed `nbf` manually. | `TokenResponse` and `WebApiRequestTests`. | Fixed | Token response now reads optional name claims safely and derives not-before from the token validity window. |
| RT-031 | Protocol parsing/emission | Distributed branch/depth messages and outgoing status/topology commands accepted negative or undefined scalar values. | Distributed branch/depth messages, status command, and message tests. | Fixed | Distributed topology scalars are now non-negative, and outgoing status values must be defined before bytes are emitted. |

| RT-033 | Protocol parsing | Several protocol boolean bytes treated any non-zero value as true or false, allowing malformed flags to alter control flow. | Login/watch/user-info/privilege/private-message/connect parsers and scalar hardening tests. | Fixed | Boolean protocol flags now accept only `0` or `1` and reject malformed values with `MessageException`; search response slot bytes remain truthy count fields for compatibility. |
| RT-034 | Example Web API request validation | Room and conversation write endpoints accepted blank usernames/messages and delegated invalid requests to the runtime. | `RoomsController`, `ConversationsController`, and `WebApiRequestTests`. | Fixed | Example write endpoints now return `400` for blank message/member bodies or blank private-message usernames. |
| RT-035 | Runtime options | Search, browse, and connection option constructors accepted impossible timeout, limit, buffer, and queue values that could fail later in network/search paths. | `SearchOptions`, `BrowseOptions`, `ConnectionOptions`, and option regression tests. | Fixed | Runtime option constructors now reject invalid scalar values at construction while preserving the documented `-1` inactivity-timeout sentinel. |
| RT-036 | Example Web API request validation | Connect and search endpoints accepted out-of-range ports and invalid search option scalars before delegating to runtime calls. | `ServerController`, `SearchesController`, and `WebApiRequestTests`. | Fixed | Example endpoints now return `400` for invalid port, timeout, limit, and filter-range values before constructing runtime options or connecting. |

| RT-042 | Runtime domain models | Public scope, file attribute, transfer, and peer queue response constructors could publish undefined enum values or negative count-like metadata that parsers and runtime state machines reject elsewhere. | `SearchScope`, `FileAttribute`, `Transfer`, `PlaceInQueueResponse`, and focused model/message tests. | Fixed | Constructors now reject undefined scope/attribute/transfer flags and negative file attribute or peer queue positions. |

| RT-044 | Transfer streams | Internal transfer progress could report infinite percentages for zero-size transfers, negative remaining bytes after over-complete progress, and accept negative peer upload start offsets. | `TransferInternal`, upload start-offset handling in `SoulseekClient`, and transfer/upload tests. | Fixed | Internal transfer progress is clamped to finite values and upload start offsets now fail before seeking or opening streams when peers send negative offsets. |
| RT-045 | Example Web API lifecycle | Web API trackers accepted invalid room message limits and null tracker payloads, allowing normal update paths to fail later with incidental collection/null exceptions. | `RoomTracker`, `ConversationTracker`, `BrowseTracker`, and tracker tests. | Fixed | Trackers now reject invalid limits/null payloads and normalize missing room message/user lists before updates. |
| RT-046 | Network lifecycle/concurrency | Empty token bucket waits ignored caller cancellation until the next timer reset and disposal could leave reset waiters unresolved. | `TokenBucket` and token bucket tests. | Fixed | Reset waits now race cancellation and disposal completes the pending reset signal with `ObjectDisposedException`. |
| RT-047 | Network lifecycle/concurrency | Invalidating an established peer message connection removed the cache record without disposing the completed connection, leaving the old socket outside manager ownership during reconnects. | `PeerConnectionManager` and peer connection manager tests. | Fixed | Cache invalidation now disposes completed cached message connections after removal while leaving unstarted/pending records untouched. |
| RT-048 | Runtime option validation | Client message timeout accepted zero or negative values that later caused immediate or invalid waiter timeout registrations. | `SoulseekClientOptions` and option tests. | Fixed | Message timeout must now be greater than or equal to one at option construction. |
| RT-049 | Transfer streams | Transfer stream writes could spin indefinitely when the input stream ended before the declared transfer length. | `Connection.WriteInternalAsync` and connection stream-write tests. | Fixed | Stream writes now fail with `ConnectionWriteException` when `ReadAsync` returns zero before the expected length is written. |
| RT-050 | Runtime option validation | Transfer maximum linger time accepted negative values that caused immediate forced disconnect behavior during upload cleanup. | `TransferOptions`, upload linger handling in `SoulseekClient`, and option tests. | Fixed | Transfer options now reject negative maximum linger values at construction. |
| RT-051 | Transfer streams | Transfer stream reads could return success with partial data when the connection was disposed between chunks before the requested length was read. | `Connection.ReadInternalAsync` and connection stream-read tests. | Fixed | Stream reads now fail with `ConnectionReadException` if the loop exits before the expected byte count is read. |
| RT-052 | Network lifecycle/concurrency | Wishlist scheduler interval calculation could throw when `ServerInfo` was unavailable from an `ISoulseekClient` implementation or when a malformed server interval exceeded `Task.Delay` bounds. | `WishlistSearchScheduler` and scheduler tests. | Fixed | Missing server info now falls back to the configured minimum interval, and oversized server intervals are capped to a delay-safe maximum. |
| RT-053 | Network lifecycle/concurrency | Enqueue upload wrappers could wait indefinitely when the transfer task completed before the local queued callback, such as cancellation before the upload semaphore path reached its queue state. | `SoulseekClient.EnqueueUploadAsync`, shared enqueue wait helper, and `EnqueueUploadAsyncTests`. | Fixed | Enqueue wrappers now race the queue signal against the transfer task and upload enqueue callbacks complete on failed terminal states. |
| RT-054 | Network lifecycle/concurrency | Upload transfer races created a linked cancellation token but passed the original caller token into long-running write and token-bucket waits, so a disconnect winner could leave the losing write path alive until unrelated cancellation/disposal. | `SoulseekClient.UploadFromStreamAsync` and upload disconnect-race tests. | Fixed | Upload stream writes and token-bucket waits now observe the linked race token, with regression coverage for disconnect-winning cancellation. |

| RT-081 | Example Web API path safety | The example shared-file cache and browse/directory resolvers advertised absolute local filesystem paths to peers, leaking host path layout and coupling remote file names to local roots. | `Extensions.GetSharedRemotePath`, `SharedFileCache`, `Startup` resolver methods, and Web API path/request tests. | Fixed | Shared file search, browse, and directory-contents responses now advertise root-relative paths while retaining root containment for incoming directory/download requests. |
| RT-082 | Example Web API lifecycle | The example shared-file cache created a new in-memory SQLite connection on every refresh without disposing the previous connection. | `SharedFileCache` and Web API path tests. | Fixed | Cache refresh now disposes the prior SQLite connection before replacing it, with regression coverage that the previous connection is closed after a refresh. |
| RT-083 | Example Web API request validation | Several example controller actions trusted blank route values after model binding, allowing empty usernames, room names, folder names, or transfer IDs to reach runtime calls or tracker lookups. | `ControllerValidation`, user/room/conversation/transfer controllers, Web API request tests, and transfer tests. | Fixed | Example controllers now reject blank route values with `400` before invoking runtime operations or tracker lookups. |
| RT-084 | Example Web API request validation | Upload lookup by username/id dereferenced the default transfer record when the upload ID was missing, returning a server error instead of `404`. | `TransfersController.GetUploads(username, id)` and transfer tests. | Fixed | Missing upload lookups now return `404` before accessing the transfer payload. |
| RT-085 | Tests/tooling | Residual small scan queues for mutable arrays, equality, and secret patterns were left as "mostly fixed" instead of being closed with countable whole-section classification. | `docs/dev/bug-council-sweep-residual-small-2026-05-05.md`, active sweep registers, and remediation-baseline checks. | Fixed | The residual sweep records `12/12`, `4/4`, and `2/2` classified with zero unclassified candidates, so future passes cannot keep rediscovering the same ambiguous small queues. |
| RT-086 | Network identity/equality | `ConnectionKey` compared usernames and computed hashes with culture-sensitive string comparison, allowing protocol identity keys such as `user` and `u\0ser` to compare equal under culture rules. | `ConnectionKey`, `WaitKey`, connection-key tests, and residual equality sweep. | Fixed | Connection identity now uses ordinal string comparison and ordinal hash codes, with regression coverage for embedded-null usernames; `WaitKey` hash codes now match its ordinal token equality. |
| RT-087 | Tests/tooling | The constructor scanner still emitted multiline declarations as multiple raw lines, so the refreshed council inventory reported `99` constructor hits even though the closed sweep owned `28` distinct constructor candidates. | `scripts/scan-bug-council-candidates.sh`, constructor sweep register, and remediation-baseline checks. | Fixed | Constructor candidate scanning now emits one normalized row per constructor declaration; the refreshed scan count matches the existing `28/28` classified sweep register. |
| RT-088 | Tests/tooling | Closed sweep registers could drift from live scanner counts because the remediation baseline checked only documented marker text, not scanner output against those markers. | `scripts/check-council-sweep-counts.sh`, `scripts/check-remediation-baseline.sh`, and `docs/dev/bug-council-scan-registry.md`. | Fixed | A dedicated sweep-count gate now runs the candidate scanner and verifies each closed section's current count still matches its dated sweep marker. |
| RT-089 | Tests/tooling | The broad protocol count/length allocation scan remained outside the closed-count gate after its subgroups were classified, so future broad-scan drift could avoid explicit council review. | `docs/dev/bug-council-sweep-protocol-length-2026-05-05.md`, `scripts/check-council-sweep-counts.sh`, and remediation-baseline checks. | Fixed | The broad protocol count/length section is now closed as `221/221` classified and enforced by the sweep-count drift gate. |
| RT-090 | Tests/tooling | The zero-hit non-idempotent task completion scan was enforced by a source absence check but was not recorded as a closed council queue, leaving future scanner drift outside the whole-section count gate. | `docs/dev/bug-council-sweep-lifecycle-2026-05-05.md`, `scripts/check-council-sweep-counts.sh`, and remediation-baseline checks. | Fixed | The lifecycle sweep now records `Non-idempotent task completion candidates: 0/0 classified`, and the sweep-count gate verifies the zero queue stays closed. |
| RT-091 | Protocol scalar emission | slskdN's vendored runtime carried negative-token and login-minor-version guards that were missing from the standalone runtime, so the two release sources could diverge and standalone protocol constructors could still emit impossible scalar identifiers. | `ProtocolArgumentValidator`, token-bearing protocol message constructors, `ProtocolScalarHardeningTests`, and the slskdN release sync pass. | Fixed | The standalone runtime now owns the token/minor-version guards, regression coverage checks every affected constructor, and the vendored runtime is synced from the standalone source of truth. |
| RT-092 | Network lifecycle/concurrency | Peer and distributed shutdown cleared pending inbound-indirect cancellation-source dictionaries without canceling or disposing the sources, allowing pending connection attempts to outlive manager shutdown. | `PeerConnectionManager`, `DistributedConnectionManager`, and manager lifecycle tests. | Fixed | Shutdown now removes, cancels, and disposes pending inbound-indirect cancellation sources before clearing active connection state. |
| RT-093 | Network lifecycle/concurrency | Overlapping inbound-indirect attempts for the same peer could overwrite the pending cancellation source, and an older attempt's cleanup could remove a newer attempt's source from cancellation ownership. | `PeerConnectionManager`, `DistributedConnectionManager`, and pending-indirect regression tests. | Fixed | Pending source registration now cancels superseded sources and cleanup removes only the matching source instance, preserving newer pending attempts. |
| RT-094 | Network lifecycle/concurrency | Reading `PeerConnectionManager.MessageConnections` evaluated lazy cached connection tasks, so observing connection state could start a connection attempt or surface a cached task failure. | `PeerConnectionManager.MessageConnections` and peer manager tests. | Fixed | Message connection snapshots now include only already-created, successfully completed cached connections and ignore pending or faulted lazy entries without evaluating them. |
| RT-095 | Wishlist scheduler lifecycle | `WishlistSearchScheduler.RunSearchAsync` caught exceptions from `SearchCompleted` event handlers as though the underlying wishlist search had failed, causing a subscriber failure after a successful search to emit a second failure completion with the subscriber exception. | `WishlistSearchScheduler` and scheduler lifecycle tests. | Fixed | Wishlist search execution is now caught separately from completion notification, so handler exceptions are no longer reclassified as search failures or emitted through duplicate failure callbacks. |
| RT-096 | Transfer snapshot progress | Public `Transfer` snapshots copied from internal transfer state calculated `BytesRemaining` as `Size - BytesTransferred` without the clamp used by `TransferInternal`, so over-complete internal progress could produce negative remaining bytes in the public API. | `Transfer`, `TransferInternal`, and transfer progress tests. | Fixed | Public transfer snapshots now clamp remaining bytes at zero, preserving the same over-complete behavior as internal transfer state and keeping remaining-time calculations non-negative. |
| RT-097 | Transfer snapshot progress | Public `Transfer` construction allowed `bytesTransferred` to be less than `startOffset`, even though runtime resumed-transfer progress treats transferred bytes as the absolute file position and `TransferInternal.StartOffset` fast-forwards transferred bytes to the offset. | `Transfer` and transfer model tests. | Fixed | Public transfer construction now rejects impossible resumed-transfer snapshots where transferred bytes are below the starting offset. |
| RT-098 | Transfer streams | Raw browse/search response constructors accepted non-readable streams, deferring an impossible response to connection-write failure after resolver ownership had already crossed into delivery paths. | `RawSearchResponse`, `RawBrowseResponse`, raw response tests, and responder/peer handler focused tests. | Fixed | Raw response construction now rejects non-readable streams at the public response boundary for both search and browse responses. |
| RT-099 | Peer capability/signature trust | Peer capability envelopes and registry records could carry undefined capability message types, and records could expose a null endpoint through registry snapshots/events. | `PeerCapabilityEnvelope`, `PeerCapabilityRecord`, registry update paths, and peer capability tests. | Fixed | Capability envelopes and records now reject undefined message types, and records require a non-null endpoint before registry publication. |
| RT-100 | Protocol emission | Many outbound string-bearing protocol constructors accepted null strings after `MessageBuilder.WriteString(null)` was hardened, creating invalid message objects that failed later during serialization. | `ProtocolArgumentValidator`, outbound server/peer/distributed/initialization message constructors, protocol emission tests, and mesh result tests. | Fixed | Outbound message constructors now reject null string arguments at construction, and mesh rendezvous result snapshots require a non-empty interest tag. |
| RT-101 | Peer capability/signature trust | Peer capability descriptors, nonces, and signature material could be constructed with feature counts or byte lengths that exceeded the envelope parser limits, producing locally emitted capability payloads that could not round-trip. | `PeerCapabilityDescriptor`, `PeerCapabilityEnvelope`, `PeerDescriptorSignature`, and peer capability tests. | Fixed | Capability descriptor construction now enforces the same feature-count, string-length, and signature byte limits used by the parser before an invalid envelope can be emitted. |
| RT-102 | Search scope validation | `SearchScope` accepted whitespace-only room and user subjects even though scoped search emission writes those values directly into room/user search protocol messages and other username/room APIs reject whitespace-only identifiers. | `SearchScope`, search scope tests, and scoped search emission paths. | Fixed | Room and user search scopes now reject null, empty, and whitespace-only subjects before scoped search requests can be emitted. |
| RT-103 | Protocol parsing | Exact-frame parsers for slskdN capability envelopes and peer initialization messages accepted valid prefixes with ignored trailing bytes, creating ambiguous parsed state for one-message payloads. | `PeerCapabilityEnvelope`, `PeerInit`, `PierceFirewall`, and parser regression tests. | Fixed | Capability envelopes now reject unread trailing bytes, and initialization `TryFromByteArray` parsers fail when any bytes remain after the declared message body. |
| RT-104 | Network metadata ownership | Runtime endpoint-bearing snapshots and event args exposed mutable `IPEndPoint` instances, allowing callers or event subscribers to mutate recorded peer, transfer, and distributed-network endpoint state after publication. | `IPEndPointExtensions`, capability records, distributed event/state snapshots, transfer snapshots, connection keys, server address responses, and endpoint ownership tests. | Fixed | Endpoint-bearing snapshots now clone endpoints on input and on read access, and connection keys keep stable hash/equality metadata even if caller-owned endpoints are later mutated. |
| RT-105 | Network metadata ownership | Runtime address-bearing options, messages, and endpoint snapshots still retained mutable IPv6 `IPAddress` references, allowing `ScopeId` mutation after construction or after property access to alter published metadata. | `IPEndPointExtensions`, server IP messages, `NetInfoNotification`, client/proxy options, listener metadata, and IP address snapshot tests. | Fixed | IP addresses are now cloned on input and on read access, endpoint snapshots clone their contained addresses, and regression tests cover IPv6 scope-id mutation across public and internal metadata surfaces. |
| RT-106 | Network lifecycle/concurrency | `ListenerHandler.HandleConnection` performed obfuscated marking and accepted-connection diagnostics before entering its initialization failure boundary, so early failures in the `async void` event handler could escape without normal diagnostic, disconnect, and dispose cleanup. | `ListenerHandler` and listener handler lifecycle tests. | Fixed | The event handler now delegates to an awaited internal task with a full-method failure boundary, and cleanup failures are swallowed after the original initialization failure is diagnosed. |
| RT-107 | Protocol parsing | `UserStatusResponseFactory` still treated any non-zero privileged byte as true after the boolean flag hardening pass, allowing malformed server status payloads to alter privileged-state snapshots. | `UserStatusResponseFactory` and protocol scalar hardening tests. | Fixed | User status privileged flags now use `ProtocolValueValidator.ValidateBooleanFlag` and reject values other than `0` or `1`. |
| RT-108 | Runtime event models | Public event snapshots for search requests, connection failures, private messages, and privilege notifications accepted negative protocol identifiers that parser and acknowledgement paths reject elsewhere. | Search/user/notification event args and event/domain model tests. | Fixed | Event args now reject negative request tokens and notification/message ids before publishing impossible identifier snapshots to subscribers. |
| RT-109 | Protocol parsing/emission | Peer and server search request messages still accepted negative search tokens and server search requests accepted null identity/query values, unlike distributed search requests and outbound search commands. | `PeerSearchRequest`, `ServerSearchRequest`, and protocol scalar tests. | Fixed | Peer and server search request constructors now reject negative tokens and null protocol strings before malformed requests can reach responder event publication. |
| RT-110 | Protocol emission | Client-generated protocol tokens could start negative when `SoulseekClientOptions.StartingToken` or `TokenFactory` was seeded with a negative value, conflicting with hardened outbound token constructors. | `TokenFactory`, `SoulseekClientOptions`, token factory/options tests, and remediation-baseline checks. | Fixed | Token generation now rejects negative starting values at both the public option boundary and internal factory boundary before generated protocol messages can fail or emit invalid identifiers. |
| RT-111 | Tests/tooling | Browse progress tests used arbitrary AutoData message lengths, allowing invalid lengths below the message-code overhead to create zero-size browse responses while still asserting 100 percent completion. | `BrowseAsyncTests` full-suite failure with generated length `3`. | Fixed | Browse progress tests now normalize generated message lengths to at least five bytes before asserting two progress updates and completion. |
| RT-112 | Runtime public API validation | Public search, directory contents, download, and upload entry points accepted explicit negative tokens even though generated tokens and outbound protocol messages now reject negative identifiers. | `SoulseekClient` token-bearing public methods and focused client regression tests. | Fixed | Added a shared client token guard so explicit negative tokens fail at the public API boundary before duplicate checks, transfer setup, or protocol message emission. |
| RT-113 | Network lifecycle/concurrency | TCP writes acquired a write-queue slot before awaiting the write semaphore, but the queue slot was outside the cleanup boundary; cancellation while waiting for the write semaphore leaked queue capacity and could cause later writes to be dropped as though the buffer were full. | `Connection.WriteInternalAsync` and TCP connection regression tests. | Fixed | Write semaphore acquisition is now inside the cleanup boundary with per-semaphore acquisition flags, preserving queue capacity when cancellation happens before a write starts while keeping full-queue disconnect behavior unchanged. |
| RT-114 | Network lifecycle/concurrency | Search token registration used a public pre-check plus unchecked internal `TryAdd`, so concurrent searches with the same token could both pass validation; the loser could continue without owning the active-search dictionary entry and then remove the winner during cleanup. | `SoulseekClient.SearchToCallbackAsync`, active search registration, and search regression tests. | Fixed | Search registration now treats `TryAdd` as authoritative, throws `DuplicateTokenException` on internal registration failure, and removes active-search entries only when the current operation registered them. |
| RT-115 | Transfer lifecycle/concurrency | Transfer token registration was split across upload and download dictionaries without an atomic cross-direction guard, so concurrent upload and download starts could register the same token even though public validation treats transfer tokens as globally unique. | `SoulseekClient` transfer registration and download/upload regression tests. | Fixed | Download and upload registration now lock the unique-key and token dictionary mutation together, reject cross-direction token collisions with `DuplicateTokenException`, and release unique keys when registration fails. |
| RT-116 | Runtime event models | `SearchResponder` raised request and delivery events directly inside responder control flow, so subscriber exceptions could abort response handling or turn successfully written search responses into failed responses. | `SearchResponder` event dispatch and responder regression tests. | Fixed | Search responder events are now raised through diagnostic boundaries so subscriber failures are logged without changing delivery/discard outcomes or skipping stream cleanup. |
| RT-117 | Peer capability negotiation | Accepted peer capability messages raised registry/client notification events before sending `Hello` acknowledgements, so subscriber exceptions could break capability negotiation after the descriptor had already been trusted and stored. | `PeerCapabilityRegistry`, `SoulseekClient.HandlePeerCapabilityMessageAsync`, and mesh rendezvous peer-message tests. | Fixed | Capability registry and client notification events now isolate subscriber exceptions; client-owned registries diagnose failures and valid `Hello` messages still produce acknowledgements. |
| RT-118 | Server protocol acknowledgements | `ServerMessageHandler` raised private-message and privilege-notification events before sending automatic acknowledgements, so subscriber exceptions could leave server messages unacknowledged even when auto-acknowledge options were enabled. | `ServerMessageHandler` and server message handler acknowledgement tests. | Fixed | Auto-acknowledged server notification events are now isolated behind diagnostics before acknowledgement decisions, preserving auto-ack behaviour when subscribers fail. |
| RT-119 | Tests/tooling | The all-phases council runner could be over-read as proof that no bugs exist because its pass text did not state the confidence boundary or run an active-discovery handoff beyond registered gates. | `scripts/run-bug-council-all-phases.sh`, `scripts/run-council-active-bughunt.sh`, `scripts/check-bug-council-all-phases.sh`, and council process docs. | Fixed | The runner now emits an explicit non-proof verdict, runs active bughunt probes every cycle, and the remediation baseline fails if the active-discovery runner or non-proof wording is removed. |
| RT-120 | Runtime event models | `DistributedConnectionManager` raised distributed topology events directly inside promotion, demotion, parent, child, and status-update control flow, so subscriber exceptions could alter distributed-network state transitions after internal state was already partially mutated. | `DistributedConnectionManager`, distributed manager event-boundary tests, active council bughunt probes, and remediation-baseline checks. | Fixed | Distributed topology callbacks now run behind diagnostic boundaries, diagnostics callbacks are isolated from runtime control flow, and regression tests cover throwing promotion, demotion, parent disconnect, child disconnect, and status-change handlers. |
| RT-121 | Runtime event models | Non-auto-ack `ServerMessageHandler` notifications still used direct event invocation inside the main message handling boundary, so subscriber exceptions were reported as server-message handling failures and could skip later side effects such as distributed-network reset cleanup. | `ServerMessageHandler`, active council unisolated-callback probe, server message handler event-boundary tests, and remediation-baseline checks. | Fixed | All server notification events now use the diagnostic event boundary, diagnostics callbacks are isolated from runtime control flow, and regression tests cover throwing server-info and distributed-reset subscribers without converting them into message handling failures. |
| RT-122 | Network event models | `MessageConnection` raised message progress, received, read, and written events directly inside connection read/write control flow, so subscriber exceptions could terminate continuous reads or turn successful writes into failed writes. | `MessageConnection`, active council unisolated-callback probe, message connection event-boundary tests, and remediation-baseline checks. | Fixed | Message connection callbacks now run through isolated helper methods, asynchronous callback dispatch also catches subscriber failures, and regression tests cover throwing `MessageDataRead`, `MessageReceived`, and `MessageWritten` subscribers. |
| RT-123 | Network event models | Low-level TCP `Connection` raised state, connected, disconnected, read-progress, and write-progress events directly inside connect, disconnect, read, and write control flow, so subscriber exceptions could fail successful network operations or prevent disconnect completion signaling. | `Connection`, active council unisolated TCP callback probe, TCP connection event-boundary tests, and remediation-baseline checks. | Fixed | TCP connection callbacks now run through isolated helper methods, asynchronous progress dispatch catches subscriber failures independently of caller cancellation, and regression tests cover throwing state, connected, disconnected, `DataRead`, and `DataWritten` subscribers. |
| RT-124 | Runtime event models | `SoulseekClient` raised lifecycle and login server-info events directly inside connect/login state transitions, so subscriber exceptions could make successful connection setup fail after state and server metadata were already updated. | `SoulseekClient`, active council unisolated client-lifecycle probe, connect lifecycle event tests, and remediation-baseline checks. | Fixed | Client lifecycle and server-info callbacks now run through diagnostic event helpers, and regression tests cover throwing `StateChanged`, `Connected`, `LoggedIn`, and `ServerInfoReceived` subscribers during a successful connect. |
| RT-125 | Runtime event models | `SoulseekClient` raised public search state and response events directly inside the search state machine and response callback, so subscriber exceptions could prevent search requests from being sent or turn valid search responses into callback failures. | `SoulseekClient`, active council unisolated client-search probe, search event-boundary tests, and remediation-baseline checks. | Fixed | Public search events now run through diagnostic event helpers while the explicit response-handler delegate remains the caller-owned result path, and regression tests cover throwing `SearchStateChanged` and `SearchResponseReceived` subscribers. |
| RT-126 | Runtime event models | `SoulseekClient` raised browse progress and transfer state/progress events directly inside browse and transfer control flow, so subscriber exceptions could fail otherwise valid browse, download, or upload operations. | `SoulseekClient`, active council unisolated client transfer/browse probe, browse and transfer event-boundary tests, and remediation-baseline checks. | Fixed | Browse progress and transfer state/progress events now run through diagnostic event helpers while operation-specific option delegates remain caller-owned callbacks, and regression tests cover throwing browse and download transfer subscribers. |
| RT-127 | Runtime event models | `SoulseekClient` directly bridged lower-level search responder, distributed manager, server handler, and diagnostic events to public subscribers, so subscriber exceptions could bubble back into message handling, connection management, or diagnostics. | `SoulseekClient`, active council unisolated bridge-event probe, constructor bridge event-boundary tests, and remediation-baseline checks. | Fixed | Constructor bridge events now route through diagnostic isolation helpers, diagnostic forwarding uses a non-recursive swallow boundary, and regression tests cover throwing search responder, distributed manager, server message, and diagnostic subscribers. |

## Verification Commands

Primary runtime verification:

```bash
bash scripts/scan-bug-council-candidates.sh
bash scripts/check-remediation-baseline.sh
dotnet test tests/Soulseek.Tests.Unit/Soulseek.Tests.Unit.csproj --no-restore
dotnet build slskNet.Runtime.sln --no-restore
dotnet list slskNet.Runtime.sln package --vulnerable --include-transitive
```

Vendored runtime verification from `../slskdn/vendor/slskNet.Runtime`:

```bash
bash scripts/scan-bug-council-candidates.sh
bash scripts/check-remediation-baseline.sh
dotnet test tests/Soulseek.Tests.Unit/Soulseek.Tests.Unit.csproj --no-restore
dotnet build slskNet.Runtime.sln --no-restore
dotnet build ../../slskd.sln --no-restore
```
